event: During Stalker FAT, aircraft 509 errored when being armed at the launch point after a completed pre-launch, because the fixed wing autopilot had failed; launch was not possible.
component: MAGACC2 board (1710P01A) in the fixed wing autopilot, under the RF shield can
failure_mode: solder ball FOD under the RF shield bridged a circuit to the shield (ground), pulling the 3.3V and 5V rails down to 2.7V and 2.5V
contributing: header soldered on manually by Edge Autonomy, creating the solder ball
no quality inspection before RF shield close-out
no conformal coating inside the can

evidence.quote: The incident maggacc board 3.3V test point is showing 2.7V. The 5.0V test point is showing 2.5V.
After powercycling the board it was noted that the 5V and 3.3V test points were back to their correct values.
FOD (solder ball) was found inside RF Shield which bridged connections
Solder ball missed by Technician prior to close out of RF Shield

team_root_cause: Quality issue.  Excessive solder balls, F.O.D. and potential corrosion was found on the component side of the magacc2 board (1710P01A), potentially as a result of missed quality check. This caused a short that inhibited functionality of the board.
reasoning: Bench measurements showed both regulator test points pulled low, and a spark near R1 while probing restored normal voltages, which fits a conductive bridge that burned clear. The customer 8D summary identifies a specific solder ball inside the RF shield from the manually soldered header as the bridge, and 17 sibling boards from the same lot were clean, supporting a one-off workmanship defect.

event: VXE 724 (preMAGNSS) MCM power cycled and rebooted when the HLB was swapped during preflight, clearing the uploaded mission; the flight was cancelled.

failure_mode: voltage transient on HLB data cable plug-in trips E-Fuse over-voltage protection, MCM supply drops below its 9 V minimum and the MCM reboots
contributing: grounding/low side issues: HLB BMS bypasses the ground isolation circuit
insufficient transient filtering on the SLA board

evidence.quote: This is not simply that the VSM process was stopped and restarted, but rather the entire MCM had been rebooted.
Initial thought is that there was a transient that exceeded the electronic fuse Over Voltage Protection that is set to 34.9V on the SLA Breakout Board V2.
I was able to test this again with another PreMAG vehicle. It actually showed the same behavior of resetting.
D5 - Impacts would be the possibly of MCM reset upon HLB data plug in for all aircraft with 128-117156-01 Rev B installed

team_root_cause: SLA Breakout 128-117156-01 Rev B has the Over Voltage Protection pin of both E-Fuses set to ~35V. When plugging in the HLB data cable, transients can occur that may briefly trip the E-Fuse protecting the MCM, which then has the possibility to drop power below the 9V minimum of the MCM.

would_settle_it.what: scope captures of the E-Fuse output during HLB plug-in showing the over-voltage trip and MCM supply dropout
schematic or setting showing the 34.9 V OVP value

reasoning: MCM uptime against AP uptime proves a true MCM power cycle on HLB swap, and the reset reproduced on a second PreMAG vehicle, so it is a design trait of the board revision rather than a one-off. The E-Fuse OVP setting of 34.9 V is a stated design value, but the trip itself is described as a hypothesis in this ticket; the measurements are said to be in VXEP-730, which is not in the files, so confidence is medium.
